Subject: Post-demo recap + pricing & perf follow-up (next tests)

Hi Emily — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we covered
- Live demo of Redwood hosted inference (multi-model catalog, streaming, tool-calls).
- Throughput/latency examples using your baseline payloads (we used 512-token prompts, see recording attached).
- High-level TCO comparison vs Hyperscaler X and OtherAPI Z (I promised a concise breakout).

Key asks from you
1) Confirm the 3 representative prompt templates (simple query, multi-turn support, long context summarization) — we used the examples you shared in the doc.
2) Target latency SLOs (p90/p95) and acceptable cold-start windows.
3) Approve the proposed 48-hour perf test window so our infra team can schedule capacity.

Attached: redwood-unit-econ-1Mtokens-vs-hyperscalers.xlsx (sample per-1M token math), demo-screen-share-20261109.mp4, proposed-poa-test-plan.pdf

Headline unit-econ summary (more detail in spreadsheet):
- Redwood (hosted, default batching + 80% KV cache) = ~$7.8 / 1M tokens (input+output).
- OtherAPI Z (managed API) = ~$14.9 / 1M tokens (no KV cache; conservative batching).
- Hyperscaler X (managed endpoint) = ~$21.5 / 1M tokens (includes per-inference infra amortization).

Notes on the math: these figures fold in model throughput, average sequence length (512 tokens), assumed batching at steady-state (6–10x effective tokens/sec improvement), and KV cache hit rate assumptions. The attached sheet shows sensitivity rows for cache hit rates (20%/50%/80%) and batch sizes (1/4/8/16).

Proposed next tests (what will give you apples-to-apples):
- 48-hour steady-state run with your three prompt templates; measure token cost, p50/p90/p95 latencies, and cache hit rate at 1, 6, and 24-hour marks.
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16 concurrent streams to validate autoscale behavior.
- Batching sensitivity: target batch windows 20ms/50ms/100ms to show cost/latency trade-offs.

If that sounds good, Monica will send a short SOW and a proposed test window. Happy to join the kickoff call.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Emily — great questions, answers below (high-level now; Monica/Jordan can provide deeper numbers):

1) Cost breakout (illustrative for 1M tokens, 512 token avg length):
- Model compute (GPU cycles): ~$5.00 / 1M tokens (our optimized kernels + batching).
- Serving infra overhead (orchestration, routing, autoscale): ~$1.80 / 1M tokens.
- Networking / egress & storage amortization: ~$0.50 / 1M tokens.
- Platform features (observability, tracing, rollouts): ~$0.50 / 1M tokens.
=> Total: ~$7.80 / 1M tokens (matches sheet).

Notes: the model compute line is where quantization and batching matter most; at higher batch sizes we amortize kernel launch costs and drop model compute to ~$3.8 / 1M tokens in our sensitivity table.

2) Short-chat prompts and cache behavior:
- Short prompts that hit identical prefixes benefit heavily from KV cache; at 80% cache hit we observe an effective token reduction of ~40–55% in GPU work (depends on model and prompt structure).
- Example: with your short-chat template (avg 64 tokens), and 80% prefix hit, our effective per-1M-token compute drops by ~45% which moves the total to ~$4.8 / 1M tokens. See the "cache-sensitivity" tab in the spreadsheet.

3) PoA (proof-of-availability) test tenancy:
- We can run the PoA in an isolated tenant in our Dedicated environment (single-tenant pool) or in hosted with strict data controls. For SOC 2 reviewers we recommend Dedicated so logs and KV caches are tenant-separated; that will be part of the SOW.

Next steps I propose this week:
- Monica to share a short SOW with test dates and the Dedicated option + cost delta.
- Emily to share three canonical prompt files and sample traffic pattern (RPS, concurrency profile).
- Jordan to confirm the exact metrics we'll collect (p50/p90/p95, tokens served, cache hit rate, batch distribution).

Monica — happy to hand off operational details to you and Jordan; once we have the sample payloads Jordan can spin up a perf run config.

Thanks — Rishi
